newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Brief profiles of Bolivia's main candidates.
newsitem.headline: Brief profiles of Bolivia's main candidates.

text.p: Bolivia's Sunday vote is likely to produce no clear winner and the future president will be picked by Congress in August from the top two candidates.
Following are brief profiles of the main three contenders:
-- GEN. HUGO BANZER seized power in 1971 and ruled with an iron fist after Ernesto (Che) Guevara's Marxist guerrillas were defeated in the late 1960s.
He has since run five times for president. Despite winning the popular vote in 1985, he failed to garner a strong-enough majority and was defeated in second-round voting in Congress.
Banzer, 71, founded his right-wing Nationalist Democratic Action (ADN) party eight months after he was toppled in 1978.
He was born in Concepcion in 1926 and married Yolanda Prada. They had five children. He sees himself as a native of the provinces who as a child studied in a small rural school.

-- Ex-President JAIME PAZ ZAMORA, of the Revolutionary Left Movement (MIR), is trying to return to office but his bid has been marred by accusations of links to drug-traffickers, which caused the United States to ban him early last year.

Although Washington says its refusal to grant him an entry visa should not interfere with domestic politics, President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada says his return to office would lead to Bolivia's international isolation.
A former revolutionary turned social democrat, Paz Zamora came third in the 1989 poll, but he took over in an unlikely alliance with his enemy and former military ruler Hugo Banzer.

Paz Zamora was born in 1939 in Cochabamba and is married to Viviana Limpias, his second wife. He has five sons from his first marriage. In 1980, he survived a plane crash caused by an attack which left permanent scars on his face and hands.

-- JUAN CARLOS DURAN, the ruling Nationalist Revolutionary Movement (MNR) hopeful, is considered the natural heir to President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada, who launched an austerity programme and privatisations in 1993.

Duran is a veteran with 15 years of parliamentary experience who climbed slowly through the MNR ranks until he was appointed deputy leader in 1993 representing the so-called "new generations" which supported Sanchez de Lozada.
A lawyer, Duran was born in La Paz 47 years ago and is married to Heidy Bohme Arze. They have two children.
